info.name: EvidenceIQ - Agent Pipeline (HTTP)
info.description:
Agent communication protocol: REST API + JSON over HTTP (FastAPI endpoints).

HOW THE AGENTS TALK
The orchestrator at /api/pipeline does not import the other agents. It calls their
REST endpoints over HTTP with JSON bodies, forwarding the caller's JWT on every
hop, exactly as the frontend would:
  Agent 1 (Criteria)     POST /api/criteria/submit
  Agent 2 (Retrieval)    POST /api/retrieval/search
  Agent 3 (Screening)    POST /api/screen
  Agent 4 (Verification) POST /api/verify

Watch the uvicorn console while running request 5: one inbound /api/pipeline/full
produces a separate inbound log line for every agent hop. That is the protocol
being demonstrated, and it is the easiest thing to show in a viva.

Agent 4 stays independent. It receives Agent 3's decision for comparison but
withholds it from its own prompt, so 'agreement: true' is a real signal.

SETUP
1. Start the backend:  cd backend && uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
2. Set the email and password collection variables to a verified account.
3. Run request 0, then request 1 (it stores the JWT), then any of the rest.

INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL (backend/.env) is where the orchestrator looks for the other
agents; it defaults to http://localhost:8000. If you run uvicorn on another port,
set it to match or the agent-to-agent calls will go to the wrong place.

Requests 2a/2b need no database. For 3a and 4a/4b set paperId and reviewId to rows
you own - copy them from the papers table in the Supabase Table Editor. Request 5
needs neither: it creates its own review through Agent 1.

COST AND RATE LIMITS
Every paper costs TWO model calls, one per agent, on two different models. Groq's
free tier caps tokens per minute, so a large run can return some papers as
VERIFICATION_FAILED or failed. Re-run it - already-screened papers are skipped by
default, so only the unfinished ones are retried.

A 502 or VERIFICATION_FAILED is usually local HTTPS interception (antivirus or a
corporate proxy) breaking the Groq connection rather than a bug. Re-run.

request.description: Run first. If this fails, uvicorn is not running.

item.name: 1. Get access token  <-- RUN THIS SECOND

request.description: Logs in against Supabase and stores access_token in the accessToken variable, which every later request uses. Set email and password first. Tokens last about an hour - re-run this when you start seeing 401s.

item.name: 2a. Run both - genuine match (expect INCLUDE / INCLUDE, agreement true)

request.description: Stateless: screens the paper with Agent 3, then hands that draft to Agent 4 for an independent re-check. Nothing is written to the database. Agent 4 never sees Agent 3's decision in its own prompt - it is compared afterwards in Python - so the two agreeing here means something. Watch the console for the per-criterion checks.

exec: pm.test("Agent 4 ran (VERIFICATION_FAILED here is usually local HTTPS interception or a Groq rate limit, not the agent - re-run)", () => pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("COMPLETE"));
pm.test("verification is present exactly when status is COMPLETE", () => pm.expect(j.verification === null).to.eql(j.status === "VERIFICATION_FAILED"));

item.name: 2b. Run both - PROMPT INJECTION (both must resist)

request.description: The security test, now across both agents. The abstract orders the model to ignore the protocol and always INCLUDE. Both agents must exclude it on its real content (mice). If either returns INCLUDE, sanitisation has regressed - treat it as a bug.

exec: pm.test("Agent 4 ran (VERIFICATION_FAILED here is usually local HTTPS interception or a Groq rate limit, not the agent - re-run)", () => pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("COMPLETE"));
pm.test("verification is present exactly when status is COMPLETE", () => pm.expect(j.verification === null).to.eql(j.status === "VERIFICATION_FAILED"));

request.description: Validation guard, same as the single-agent endpoints.
The pipeline runs on behalf of a known user, never anonymously.

item.name: 3a. One stored paper - writes BOTH agents' columns

request.description: Loads the paper and its review's protocol, runs both agents, and writes draft_decision/draft_reason/screened_at AND verified_decision/confidence/agreement/needs_human_review/verification_note/checks/issues/verified_at back to the row. paperId must belong to a review YOU own or this returns 403. If Agent 4 fails, the screening columns are still saved and status comes back VERIFICATION_FAILED - a second opinion timing out should not throw away a good first opinion.

exec: pm.test("Agent 4 ran (VERIFICATION_FAILED here is usually local HTTPS interception or a Groq rate limit, not the agent - re-run)", () => pm.expect(j.status).to.eql("COMPLETE"));
pm.test("verification is present exactly when status is COMPLETE", () => pm.expect(j.verification === null).to.eql(j.status === "VERIFICATION_FAILED"));

request.description: A paper id that does not exist.
The ownership check. This seeded paper belongs to a fake owner id no real account matches, so any genuine login must be refused.

item.name: 4a. Whole review - screen and verify every paper

request.description: Runs both agents over every paper in the review that has not been screened yet, a few at a time, and saves the lot in one transaction. Papers already screened are skipped so calling this twice does not spend your model quota twice - add ?rerun=true to force them. One paper failing does not sink the run: its slot carries an error and the rest are still saved. Check 'disagreements' - those are the papers where Agent 4 reached a different conclusion than Agent 3, and the ones a researcher should look at first.

exec: pm.test("every paper is accounted for", () => pm.expect(j.complete + j.verification_failed + j.failed).to.eql(j.total));
pm.test("screening counts add up", () => pm.expect(j.included + j.excluded).to.eql(j.complete + j.verification_failed));

request.description: Same as 4a but re-processes papers that already have a screening decision. Costs two model calls per paper, so use it when the protocol changed, not by habit.
A review id that does not exist.

The whole system in one call, and the clearest demonstration of the agent communication protocol.

Agent 1 turns the prose criteria into a structured protocol and creates the review. Agent 2 searches PubMed and stores the papers. Agents 3 and 4 then screen and verify each one. Every arrow there is an HTTP POST to another agent's endpoint - watch the uvicorn console.

Agent 1 is allowed to stop the chain: if your criteria are ambiguous it returns a clarifying question instead of a protocol, and the response comes back with clarification_needed=true and stopped_at='Agent 1 (Criteria)'. That is the system working correctly, not a failure - screening against a protocol the researcher never confirmed would produce confident wrong answers. Make the criteria vaguer (say 'diabetes' with no type) to see it.

Keep max_results small. Each paper costs two model calls.

exec: console.log("stopped_at:", j.stopped_at || "none - all four agents ran");
pm.test("Agent 1 stopped the chain with a question", () => pm.expect(j.question).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty);
pm.test("every paper is accounted for", () => pm.expect(s.complete + s.verification_failed + s.failed).to.eql(s.total));
pm.test("the chain ran to the end", () => pm.expect(j.stopped_at).to.be.null);
